findings.title: Security (surface 5): injection
findings.body:
Reachability: Feishu event payload field event.message.content -> parsed at service/feishu_finance_agent.go:319-320 (`_ = common.UnmarshalJsonStr(msg.Content, &content)` / `text := strings.TrimSpace(feishuMentionPlaceholder.ReplaceAllString(content.Text, ""))`) -> persisted as action.RawText (feishu_finance_agent.go:334) -> reloaded at feishu_finance_agent.go:350 (`text := action.RawText`) -> passed to parseFeishuFinanceAgentCommand at feishu_finance_agent.go:359 -> placed verbatim as the LLM user message here (client.go:286) -> POSTed to the LLM at client.go:349 (`cfg.LLMBaseURL+"/chat/completions"`). The LLM's JSON output (target_account, commission_rate_percent, commission_window_days, withdraw_enabled, gift_credits) becomes the execution plan.
Note: Prompt injection into the LLM engine: attacker-influenced text (third-party content the operator pastes or quotes; the code's own threat-model comment states 消息原文不可信) is interpreted as instructions, so injected text can steer the parsed command toward a different target account or maximal values (gift credits up to 1,000,000, commission up to 50%). Mitigations exist but do not break reachability: sender must pass whitelist + live Root check (authorizeFeishuFinanceAgentOperator), values are clamped server-side in buildFeishuFinanceAgentPlan, and execution requires the originating operator to click confirm on a card that echoes the raw text with injection hints (feishuFinanceAgentInjectionWarningText); only that human confirmation stands between a fully injected plan and the write calls AddAffPromotionUsers/GrantAdminCredits.
findings.recommendation: Fix the issue, or provide evidence that the path is not reachable.

findings.title: Security (surface 7): SSRF
findings.body:
Reachability: Source: env var FEISHU_FINANCE_AGENT_OPENAPI_BASE read via os.Getenv at setting/feishu_finance_agent_setting.go:32 -> cached by setting.GetFeishuFinanceAgentSetting() -> StartFeishuFinanceAgentWS -> runFeishuFinanceAgentWSSession(cfg) -> feishuFinanceAgentWSDomain(cfg.OpenAPIBase) -> sink: larkws.WithDomain(domain) at service/feishu_finance_agent_ws.go:102, consumed by larkws.NewClient(cfg.AppID, cfg.AppSecret, opts...) and client.Start(context.Background()) at lines 105-106, which dials the derived host.
Note: The outbound long-connection host is taken verbatim from a deployment environment variable with no allowlist or scheme/host validation (feishuFinanceAgentWSDomain only trims whitespace, a trailing '/' and the '/open-apis' suffix), and the setting file comment explicitly states this base can be pointed at an arbitrary fake service. The same client then authenticates to whatever host is configured using cfg.AppID/cfg.AppSecret, so whoever can influence this env var redirects the connection and exfiltrates the Feishu app credentials. The same env-controlled-URL pattern exists for FEISHU_FINANCE_AGENT_LLM_BASE_URL (setting/feishu_finance_agent_setting.go:33) paired with FEISHU_FINANCE_AGENT_LLM_API_KEY, but its HTTP sink lives in service/feishu_finance_agent_client.go whose content is not in the supplied diff, so it is folded into this row instead of reported separately. The source is deployment configuration (env) rather than end-user request data, which is the only reason this is not rated higher.
findings.recommendation: Fix the issue, or provide evidence that the path is not reachable.

notes: Verification statements (not claims): the author reports 20 new/updated tests covering plan building, full confirmation flow, duplicate clicks, non-initiator/demoted Root, cancel/expiry, stranger handling, SDK event and card-callback conversion, executing re-click, crash recovery, json_schema->json_object fallback, command JSON field validation, injection warnings, replay re-auth, fencing, parsing recovery, and withdrawal re-read; go build ./... and go test ./service ./model ./router ./controller reportedly pass; a real-model retest (deepseek-v4.1-flash) and a local end-to-end smoke with a real Feishu app were run.
The author explicitly states the threat model (LLM produces plan only; human Root confirmation is the sole execution gate) requires Root-side acceptance before relying on it.
The author notes multiple backend instances may share one Feishu app with events randomly distributed, relying on DB dedup and state preemption for single execution.
The author notes a local SQLite development caveat with glebarez v1.10 restart DDL behavior, stated as unrelated to this PR (production uses PostgreSQL).

Configuration is via environment variables (FEISHU_FINANCE_AGENT_APP_ID, FEISHU_FINANCE_AGENT_APP_SECRET, FEISHU_FINANCE_AGENT_LLM_BASE_URL, FEISHU_FINANCE_AGENT_LLM_API_KEY, FEISHU_FINANCE_AGENT_LLM_MODEL, optional FEISHU_FINANCE_AGENT_OPENAPI_BASE); required Feushu permissions are listed as im:message:send_as_bot, im:message.p2p_msg:readonly, im:message.group_at_msg:readonly.
No linked issues were supplied and the reviewer-comments section is empty, so there is no evidence for maintainer overlap.

All 13 changed files are additions (no deletions), consistent with a new feature; claims about second-round fixes (F1-F6, S5+Q7, Q30, Q13, Q4) are author assertions in the PR body and were not verified against a diff in this phase.
This slice covers only go.mod, go.sum, main.go, model/feishu_finance_agent.go and model/main.go; claims implemented in service/* and setting/* files are omitted here, not refuted.
Several delivered entries (c1, c2, c4, c8) rest partly on comments in model/feishu_finance_agent.go and main.go; runtime enforcement for those behaviors is not present in this slice.
go.sum/go.mod indirect additions (e.g. github.com/gogo/protobuf, golang.org/x/* old go.mod hashes) look like transitive dependencies of the lark SDK; no unrelated changes found in this slice.
c3, c4, c6, c13 depend on files outside this slice (feishu_finance_agent_ws.go, setting/, model/, main.go); no verdict emitted for them here.

This slice shows the official SDK github.com/larksuite/oapi-sdk-go/v3 used for Reply and PatchMessage (service/feishu_finance_agent_client.go lines 19-21), consistent with c3, but the long-connection listener itself is not in this slice.
Line ranges point into the new-file hunks as shown in the diff; SQL-level constraints (unique source_message_id, exec_version predicate) are only visible here through model function names.

All line numbers are derived from the new-file hunks in this slice. c5 and c19 are omitted: the model call sites (AddAffPromotionUsers / GrantAdminCredits with feishu-<actionID> request id) and the json_schema -> json_object fallback are in files not included in this slice.

Behavior constants (30-minute card expiry, 2.5s card deadline, 60s replay timeout, 500-char command cap, 5-minute maintenance cadence, 100 rows x 10 batches) are only exercised indirectly by tests here; their definitions live in service/feishu_finance_agent.go outside this slice.

TestFeishuFinanceAgentRejectsTargetNotInText (service/feishu_finance_agent_test.go 263-272) shows an unstated safety rule: the parsed target account must literally appear in the raw message, otherwise the action is marked Ignored with a text reply; minor and consistent with the anti-injection design in c18.

service/feishu_finance_agent_ws.go constructs the dispatcher with empty verification token and encrypt key (dispatcher.NewEventDispatcher("", "")), which is consistent with long-connection mode (c3) rather than a gap.
setting/feishu_finance_agent_setting.go exposes SetFeishuFinanceAgentSettingForTest, a test-only injection hook in a production package; minor, not flagged as creep.
